function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person at a single moment; it emerged gradually as a series of observations, experiments, and theoretical breakthroughs over many centuries. Here’s a quick tour of some of the most influential figures:

| Time | Key Contributions | Why They Matter |
|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **c. 600 BCE – Thales of Miletus** | Noted that rubbing amber produced static attraction. | First recorded observation of static electricity. |
| **c. 1600 – William Gilbert** | Published *De Magnete*, distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coined the term “electricus.” | Laid the groundwork for systematic study of electrical phenomena. |
| **mid‑1700s – Benjamin Franklin** | Conducted the famous kite experiment, showing that lightning is electrical. Introduced the concepts of positive/negative charge and the conservation of charge. | Demonstrated the electrical nature of lightning and helped popularize the field. |
| **1791 – Alessandro Volta** | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), providing a steady source of electric current. | Enabled controlled experiments and practical applications. |
| **1800s – Michael Faraday** | Discovered electromagnetic induction and formulated Faraday’s laws of induction. | Paved the way for electric generators and motors. |
| **1831 – James Clerk Maxwell** | Unified electricity and magnetism into a single theory of electromagnetism. | Provided the theoretical framework that underpins all modern electrical engineering. |

Other notable contributors include Luigi Galvani (bioelectricity), André-Marie Ampère (electromagnetism), and many others who refined measurement techniques and built early electrical devices.

So, while no single person “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these pioneers—and countless others—transformed it from a curious static phenomenon into the cornerstone of modern technology.
